scenario: paired A/B for the EnvironmentIds memo (D-134)

topology.note: pre-change binary on 127.0.0.1:58091 and post-change binary on 127.0.0.1:58095, identical environment (colophon_perf, shared Valkey), alternating k6 iterations so ambient load applies equally to both

method: constant-arrival-rate 100/s for 45s; iteration n hits the old binary when n is even, the new when odd; per iteration 60% /media/v1/{p}/production/{asset}/w320, 20% /w1280, 20% /content/v1/.../posts?limit=5; `list` is the control — its code path is unchanged, so old-vs-new equality there shows the pairing controls ambient, and a media delta is the memo's. Both servers warmed first (every asset's w320/w1280 and the list page).
ambient_caveat: The laptop's load average was ~70-90 during both runs (a VM, storage services and unrelated builds shared the 12 cores), so absolute latencies are inflated versus the quiet baseline at 2026-11-05T013738Z; the old-vs-new pairing is what the numbers prove.

run_2.note: ambient load higher than run_1 — the pairing still controls it

verdict.control_identical: list med old==new in both runs (2.54/2.53; 13.10/13.13) — the pairing controls ambient
verdict.database_transactions: the 300/s audience-sites steady run dropped 19,487 -> 9,601 (-51%) on the same 18k-request mix: media's per-request delivery_environment lookup is gone
verdict.conclusion: the memo removes the delivery_environment round trip (one Postgres RT through the Docker port mapping, ~0.7 ms here) plus one transaction from every media request — over half the mix; under heavier ambient the absolute saving grows because a queued round trip costs more, the structural saving is identical
